2025-02-25

Why was there no provisioning before 11am?

Previously, we noticed there was a strange cutoff for provisioning. It was an accidental result of the temp matching process - time zone was not handled properly and so temps were matched to the wrong times.

Provis by time of day: WEBL, 1h

So now provisioning and temp actually both line up in a way that seems reasonable. Yay!

Provis by time of day: TRES

Plot raw data for WEBL

Looks like a lot of the outliers are in forest. Wondering if this could be caused by moving leaves being detected as birds??

First task: Figure out what distribution to use for modeling these data.

This looks like a poisson distribution would do okay here. But I will start with a Gaussian distribution for completeness.

Base model with Gaussian distribution, qqplot

##        aic    bic r2.conditional r2.marginal       icc    rmse nobs
## 1 2272.722 2347.9      0.4159197   0.1938775 0.2754448 8.83681  317

Base model with Poisson distribution, qqplot

## High Correlation

##          poly(mean_temp_scaled, 2) 17.47 [14.32, 21.37]         4.18      0.06
##  poly(mean_temp_scaled, 2):habitat 17.75 [14.55, 21.71]         4.21      0.06
##  Tolerance 95% CI
##      [0.05, 0.07]
##      [0.05, 0.07]

The Poisson distribution addresses the zero skewing but not the overdispersion?

Test for overdispersion

##        aic      bic r2.conditional r2.marginal      icc     rmse nobs
## 1 2849.936 2921.355      0.8658983   0.3327908 0.799011 8.154948  317
## # Overdispersion test
## 
##        dispersion ratio =    5.835
##   Pearson's Chi-Squared = 1738.790
##                 p-value =  < 0.001
## # Check for zero-inflation
## 
##    Observed zeros: 40
##   Predicted zeros: 6
##             Ratio: 0.15

So, we do have overdispersion and zero inflation.

Let’s try binomial distribution

##        aic      bic r2.conditional r2.marginal       icc      rmse nobs
## 1 3229.778 3301.197      0.2036256  0.08140831 0.1330486 0.0928431  317
## # Overdispersion test
## 
##  dispersion ratio = 2.296
##           p-value = 0.024

Dispersion ratio is smaller than for Poisson, but still doesn’t fully account for overdispersion.

Negative binomial

##       aic      bic r2.conditional r2.marginal       icc     rmse nobs
## 1 2105.11 2180.288      0.5446711   0.2263164 0.4114792 8.892014  317
## # Overdispersion test
## 
##  dispersion ratio = 0.968
##           p-value = 0.784
## # Check for zero-inflation
## 
##    Observed zeros: 40
##   Predicted zeros: 22
##             Ratio: 0.56

Negative binomial seems to address overdispersion and help with zeroinflation. If we add a zeroinflation term, what happens?

Zero inflation model

##        aic      bic r2.conditional r2.marginal       icc    rmse nobs
## 1 2081.786 2160.723      0.8043761   0.4964552 0.6115064 8.87989  317
## # Overdispersion test
## 
##  dispersion ratio = 0.951
##           p-value = 0.752
## # Check for zero-inflation
## 
##    Observed zeros: 40
##   Predicted zeros: 37
##             Ratio: 0.92
## Warning: Non-uniformity of simulated residuals detected (p = 0.019).

Test for overdispersion and zeroinflation are negative, but there appears to be some non-uniformity of residuals. Poisson instead of negative binomial results in more overdispersion.

Looks like there are some outliers. I wonder if we can justify clipping off outliers - does it make sense for birds to visit more than 60x/hour? I suspect some of those videos are from birds sitting in the entrance the whole time.

Rows with > 60 visits/hour clipped.

##        aic      bic r2.conditional r2.marginal       icc     rmse nobs

##  dispersion ratio = 0.977
##           p-value = 0.912
## # Check for zero-inflation
## 
##    Observed zeros: 40
##   Predicted zeros: 38
##             Ratio: 0.96
## OK: Simulated residuals appear as uniformly distributed (p = 0.078).

Still some funkiness, and fat tails. Still some non-uniformity.

Conclusions:

High temps do appear to depress provisioning behavior. Looks like the squared term interaction is supported in the overall model.

Provis by time of day: TRES, 1h

So now provisioning and temp actually both line up in a way that seems reasonable. Yay!

Plot raw data for TRES

Looks like way higher average detection for TRES. I’m a little worried that TRES data is inflated because they are much more likely to sit in the hole of the nest. I think I would have to build another classification model to identify those videos, though it would certainly be possible.

First task: Figure out what distribution to use for modeling these data.

This looks like a Poisson distribution would be overdispersed. But I’ll run through all of the other distributions for completeness.

##  poly(mean_temp_scaled, 2):habitat 6164.64 [4872.83, 7798.98]        78.52
##  Tolerance Tolerance 95% CI
##   3.52e-04     [0.00, 0.00]
##   1.62e-04     [0.00, 0.00]

Test for overdispersion

##       aic      bic r2.conditional r2.marginal      icc     rmse nobs
## 1 2633.47 2698.876      0.9616209   0.4911621 0.924575 9.348511  231
## # Overdispersion test
## 
##        dispersion ratio =    7.820
##   Pearson's Chi-Squared = 1657.933
##                 p-value =  < 0.001
## # Check for zero-inflation
## 
##    Observed zeros: 42
##   Predicted zeros: 7
##             Ratio: 0.17

So, we do have overdispersion and zero inflation.

Let’s try binomial distribution

##        aic      bic r2.conditional r2.marginal      icc      rmse nobs
## 1 3121.358 3186.764      0.4585998   0.2336588 0.293526 0.1436397  231
## # Overdispersion test
## 
##  dispersion ratio = 0.771
##           p-value =   0.4

Dispersion ratio is accounted for, but model doesn’t converge- probably the zero inflation.

Negative binomial

##       aic      bic r2.conditional r2.marginal       icc     rmse nobs
## 1 1683.83 1752.679      0.5034279   0.2410555 0.3457069 9.985896  231
## # Overdispersion test
## 
##  dispersion ratio = 0.325
##           p-value = 0.048
## # Check for zero-inflation
## 
##    Observed zeros: 42
##   Predicted zeros: 22
##             Ratio: 0.52

Negative binomial seems to address overdispersion and help with zeroinflation. If we add a zeroinflation term, what happens?

Zero inflation model (~1)

##        aic      bic r2.conditional r2.marginal       icc     rmse nobs
## 1 1616.703 1688.994      0.8790488   0.6515396 0.6528983 11.06691  231
## # Overdispersion test
## 
##  dispersion ratio = 0.879
##           p-value = 0.712
## # Check for zero-inflation
## 
##    Observed zeros: 42
##   Predicted zeros: 43
##             Ratio: 1.03
## OK: Simulated residuals appear as uniformly distributed (p = 0.577).

Test for overdispersion and zeroinflation are negative, and residuals seem uniformly distributed. Are we good to go?

Overall conclusions:

Having the squared term in the model doesn’t improve fit and increases the size of standard errors… I think
